papers.title: Autism mutations rewire protein interaction networks to drive neurodevelopmental pathology.
papers.summary: Affinity purification-mass spectrometry mapped protein-protein interactions (PPIs) for 100 high-confidence autism (ASD) genes, uncovering >1800 interactions. Pathogenic missense mutations cause convergent PPI rewiring onto shared complexes; distinct patient-derived FOXP1 variants disrupt FOXP4 binding, altering cortical neurogenesis and neural activity in brain organoids — linking genetic variation to convergent neurodevelopmental pathology.

papers.title: A tripartite genetic conflict system controls hybrid sterility in rice.
papers.summary: The rice gene RHS3 is a major QTL controlling hybrid sterility and encodes a tripartite toxin-antidote system (MAO, DUN, JIA). MAO acts as a toxin aborting gametes by disrupting mitochondrial function; DUN and JIA neutralize it via selective autophagy through a JIA-DUN-MAO complex. Its de novo origin in AA-genome rice links genetic conflict to speciation and suggests strategies to harness Asian-African rice heterosis.

papers.title: SGLT2 inhibitors activate pantothenate kinase in the human heart.
papers.summary: SGLT2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) directly activate pantothenate kinase 1 (PANK1), the rate-limiting enzyme in coenzyme A synthesis. Stable-isotope infusions confirmed activation of CoA synthesis and broad fuel use in human cardiac tissue; the PANK1 binding site was modeled and mutagenesis-verified. PANK activation is necessary and sufficient to increase human cardiomyocyte contractility — an off-target mechanism that may explain SGLT2i clinical benefits.

papers.title: Nonviral delivery of chemically modified tRNA rescues nonsense mutations in cystic fibrosis.
papers.summary: Chemically modified suppressor tRNAs combining N1-methyladenosine incorporation with cargo-tailored pulmonary lipid nanoparticles rescued nonsense mutations. The modifications improved premature-termination-codon readthrough, tRNA aminoacylation, functional persistence, and reduced innate immune activation. This platform delivered engineered suppressor tRNAs to the lung and restored CFTR expression and function in bronchial epithelial cells, mouse models, and patient-derived organoids.

papers.title: A necroptotic-to-apoptotic signaling axis underlies inflammatory bowel disease.
papers.summary: Aberrant epithelial cell death signaling was identified as an underlying feature of IBD that persists in patients in remission and on advanced therapy. Nascent inflammation skews epithelial cells into an M1-macrophage-like state promoting RIPK1-independent necroptosis, which triggers iNOS-assisted mitochondrial apoptosis of absorptive cells and PUMA-mediated intestinal stem cell death — a hallmark predictive of clinical relapse.

papers.title: Disruption of mitonuclear coadaptation and compensatory evolution after an extreme dietary shift in carnivorous butterflies.
papers.summary: Carnivorous miletinae butterflies with an extreme dietary shift show a reversed mitonuclear evolutionary response: elevated mitochondrial nucleotide substitution (driven by relaxed purifying selection) while nuclear rates stay stable. The nuclear genome underwent pervasive, multilayered compensatory evolution across OXPHOS complexes, mitochondrial translation/replication machinery, and homeostasis systems — supporting that extreme ecological shifts disrupt mitonuclear coadaptation and drive systemic nuclear compensation.

papers.title: Combined type 2 cytokine blockade enhances PD-1-mediated antitumor immunity.
papers.summary: Combined blockade of type 2 cytokines IL-4, IL-13, and TSLP enhanced PD-1-mediated antitumor immunity. In CT26 and KP787 tumor models, combined blockade plus PD-1 inhibition improved tumor growth control and reprogrammed T cells, monocytes, and dendritic cells toward antitumor phenotypes. Across human cancer datasets, IL-4/IL-13/TSLP activity signatures correlated with poorer survival, supporting therapeutic targeting of this suppressive axis.

papers.title: Heterogeneous single-cell dynamics support stable population codes for objects in the mouse anterior cingulate cortex.
papers.summary: Longitudinal calcium imaging in freely moving mice tracked ACC excitatory neurons exploring objects across days. Although the proportion of object-responsive neurons stayed constant, the identity of those cells fluctuated with continuous turnover around a small stable core; high-exploring mice showed greater cellular stability. Population-level decoding became linearly separable — stable spatial representations emerge from collective, emergent network organization despite persistent single-cell dynamics.

papers.title: Interleukin-17A-producing γδ T cells drive cognitive dysfunction in periodontitis.
papers.summary: Porphyromonas gingivalis-induced periodontitis promoted anxiety-like behavior and progressive cognitive dysfunction in mice. IL-17A-producing T cells accumulated in the mouth, and an increased Vγ4+ γδ T-cell population migrated to the brain via draining cervical lymph nodes through the CCL20/CCR6 pathway. Anti-IL-17A, anti-CCL20, or anti-TCRγδ antibody treatment ameliorated both behavioral deficits — an IL-17A-mediated oral-brain axis linking periodontitis to cognitive dysfunction.

papers.title: An in vivo resource of age-regulated C. elegans intestinal secretory-pathway proteins highlights secreted enzymes associated with lifespan regulation.
papers.summary: Proximity labeling plus quantitative proteomics systematically characterized C. elegans intestinal secretory-pathway proteins, identifying age-modulated secreted proteins validated in vivo. The human-conserved secreted protein ACP7, a phosphatase active in the extracellular space, extends lifespan in a secretion-dependent manner when overexpressed. Additional secretory-pathway proteins regulate lifespan — a resource of conserved extracellular enzymes tied to aging.

papers.title: Maternal microbiome promotes offspring ovarian reserve via bile acid metabolism.
papers.summary: Maternal antibiotic-induced microbiome disruption in mice caused diminished ovarian reserve (DOR) in offspring, which fecal microbiota transplantation alleviated. Disruption altered maternal serum metabolomes with reduced bile-acid secretion; supplementation of key bile-acid metabolites or transplantation of Lactobacillus gasseri to antibiotic-treated dams abrogated DOR and improved oocyte quality — maternal microbiome → bile-acid metabolism → offspring fertility.

papers.title: Biogenesis of virus-derived piRNAs in Bombyx mori BmN4 cells: Evidence for incidental processing of viral RNA.
papers.summary: Bioinformatic analysis of small-RNA-seq data characterized Bombyx mori latent virus-derived piRNAs in BmN4 cells: predominantly sense-oriented, 27-28 nt, 2'-O-methylated, bound by both Siwi and Ago3, and dependent on trimmer for 3' maturation, lacking ping-pong signatures. Zucchini processes viral RNA into ~70-90 nt intermediates without nucleotide bias — vpiRNAs likely emerge as incidental byproducts of piRNA machinery processing abundant viral transcripts, not a dedicated antiviral response.

papers.title: ISL1 regulates the differentiation and maintenance of dental epithelial stem cells in the incisor.
papers.summary: Ablation of ISL1 in dental epithelium via Pitx2-Cre impaired mandibular incisor development — reduced size, decreased epithelial/mesenchymal proliferation, and increased apoptosis in the lateral cervical loop. ISL1 deletion upregulated Hedgehog (Shh, Ptch1, Gli1) and FGF (Fgf3, Etv4, Etv5) mediators while downregulating stem-cell markers Sox2 and Lgr5. ISL1 colocalizes with and regulates Sox2, sustaining dental epithelial stem-cell viability and orchestrating ameloblast lineage commitment.

papers.title: The non-canonical CDK2 activator SPY1 uses separable mechanisms to activate phosphorylated and unphosphorylated CDK2.
papers.summary: The non-canonical CDK2 activator SPY1 activates both phosphorylated and unphosphorylated CDK2 with efficacy similar to cyclin A. FRET shows SPY1 binding induces a CDK2 conformational shift of similar magnitude to cyclin A regardless of phosphorylation state, and allosterically enhances ATP-competitive CDK2 inhibitor binding. The D136A mutant is inactive toward unphosphorylated CDK2 yet still activates phosphorylated CDK2 — functional non-equivalence of two activation mechanisms.

papers.title: Pervasive context-dependent effects in the genetic architecture of complex and quantitative traits revealed by a powerful multiparent mapping population in yeast.
papers.summary: The CYCLONES multiparent yeast population (9,344 haploid strains, eight founders) identified 349 QTL explaining 60-100% of narrow-sense heritability across ten growth conditions. Growth traits showed condition-specific architectures with extensive allelic heterogeneity; a PCA1 cadmium-transporter QTL explains 72% of cadmium-resistance variation, and a GAL3-introgression interaction extends a known GAL-pathway incompatibility to a four-locus interaction.

papers.title: DDI-4 induces a temperature-sensitive exocytotic remodeling during C. elegans spermiogenesis via nsun-2-dependent sphingosine signaling.
papers.summary: DDI-4, a benzylamine analog, induces membrane organelle fusion (MOF) in C. elegans sperm and the analogous mammalian acrosome reaction, revealing shared sensitivity. Elevated-temperature spermatids showed selective impairment of DDI-4-induced MOF. Forward genetics linked the nyg20 phenotype to nsun-2 (tRNA methyltransferase) function; sphingosine kinases are candidate targets, with sphk-1 loss phenocopying the nsun-2 mutant — suggesting sphk-1 acts as both kinase and scaffold for temperature-sensitive exocytotic remodeling.

papers.title: Ingression of the cardiac outflow tract wall is disrupted in mice with altered β-catenin, Shh and FGF8 signaling.
papers.summary: scRNA-seq of E10.5 mouse outflow tract (OFT) identified Nkx2-5 expression in the inferior midline OFT wall and adjacent intercalated valve swellings (ICVS). OFT wall cells ingress while maintaining myocyte properties, with leading cells transitioning to a mesenchymal fate via 'lily-bulb' collective migration; β-catenin, Shh, and FGF8 signaling associate with ICVS formation — new insight into second heart field-driven OFT septation and congenital heart disease.

papers.title: Establishment of a patient-derived malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor organoid model reveals SHH pathway activation and therapeutic vulnerability.
papers.summary: A stable patient-derived organoid line from a malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor (MPNST), established via a modified air-liquid interface method, along with an organoid-derived xenograft, retained the original tumor's histology, phenotype, and genome. Both cases shared NF1/SUZ12 copy-number alterations; the organoid-forming case had PTCH1 loss-of-function and SHH pathway activation, and vismodegib significantly suppressed organoid growth — identifying SHH as a therapeutically actionable vulnerability.

papers.title: Atypical PI3Ks coordinate chemotaxis, signaling dynamics, and multicellular development in Dictyostelium.
papers.summary: Three atypical PI3K-family enzymes — PikF, PikG, and PikH — define genetically separable functions in Dictyostelium. PikF attenuates Ras-phosphoinositide-actin signaling to spatially and temporally constrain protrusion; PikG is required for aggregation and supports Aca-dependent cAMP relay; PikH supports efficient phagocytic uptake with little effect on acute signaling. This expands the Dictyostelium PI3K framework beyond class-I PI(3,4,5)P3-centered pathways.

papers.title: Targeted ATAC-see (tATAC-see): A visual assay for target-specific chromatin profiling.
papers.summary: Targeted ATAC-see (tATAC-see) integrates in situ ATAC-see visualization with antibody-tethered tagmentation for site-specific chromatin profiling. Salt titration of the Tn5 spatial interaction radius enables extended tagmentation of local chromatin; validation captured H3K27ac/H3K4me3 euchromatin neighborhoods and lamin A/C and lamin B1 lamina-associated domains, tracked HDAC-inhibitor decompaction, and revealed divergent LAD/chromatin trajectories in replicative, chronological, and Hutchinson-Gilford progeria aging models.

papers.title: The First Highly Contiguous Genome Assembly for the Western bluebird (Sialia mexicana).
papers.summary: The first high-quality de novo reference genome for the Western bluebird (Sialia mexicana): a PacBio HiFi-derived, highly contiguous phased 1.3 Gb assembly with a contig N50 of 24.8 Mb, 98.3% BUSCO completeness, and 16,656 annotated protein-coding genes, plus a complete ~16 kb mitochondrial genome. This provides a foundational resource for population, connectivity, demographic-history, and conservation genomics studies.

papers.title: Genomic evidence of early-diverging domesticated lineages in Norwegian farmhouse yeast.
papers.summary: Whole-genome sequencing of 64 kveik isolates from 25 traditional Norwegian brewing cultures, with telomere-to-telomere assemblies, shows kveik forms a paraphyletic, early-diverging lineage among domesticated S. cerevisiae, with low within-culture diversity, strong geographic clustering, and little gene flow. Reported kveik-Asian gene-flow signals are likely artifacts of population structure; the common ancestor of beer, kveik, and liquid-fermenting strains arose ~4,000-8,000 years ago — among the oldest domesticated lineages in continuous use.

papers.title: Little sharks in a genomic world: A high-resolution view of population structure in the California horn shark (Heterodontus francisci).
papers.summary: ddRADseq genotyping of 3,953 nuclear SNPs from 175 California horn sharks (Heterodontus francisci) identified at least five genetically distinct population units, recovering strong differentiation between the northern Channel Islands and Santa Catalina Island and supporting deep-water channels as dispersal barriers at scales as small as 20 km (FST ≥0.020). Shallow structure tracked geography over >1,200 km of coastline, with reduced diversity in island populations — supporting stock-specific management.

papers.title: Translophagy-A potential link between autophagy impairment and translational errors.
papers.summary: Proteomic analysis of ubiquitin-enriched and p62-associated fractions in autophagy-deficient tissue confirmed ribosomal proteins and RNA-binding factors among candidate autophagy cargo. Pharmacological or genetic impairment of autophagy increased translational errors, particularly under oxidative stress; translational machinery localized to LC3-positive autophagic structures and accumulated in neurodegeneration-affected human brain. This supports 'translophagy' — autophagy preserving protein-synthesis quality by removing damaged translational machinery.

papers.title: HDAC2 restrains IGF2BP1-associated m6A dysregulation in cervical cancer immunotherapy resistance.
papers.summary: The m6A reader IGF2BP1 is upregulated in cervical cancer and correlates with poor survival; knockdown suppresses proliferation and sensitizes tumors to anti-PD-1 by enhancing CD8+ T-cell infiltration and IFNγ secretion. IGF2BP1 stabilizes immunosuppressive and stemness transcripts (PD-L1, WNT4, POU5F1, MYC) via m6A-dependent processing, while HDAC2 represses IGF2BP1 transcription by erasing H3K27ac marks at its promoter — an HDAC2/IGF2BP1/m6A axis in immunotherapy resistance.

papers.title: First cell-patterning of primary, patient-derived mesenchymal glioblastoma brain cancer cells on parylene-C/SiO2 substrates.
papers.summary: Two patient-derived mesenchymal glioblastoma cell lines were patterned onto grid networks of biocompatible parylene-C on SiO2 substrates, optimizing node size, spacing, and track length via five patterning indices. Patterned cells responded to ATP stimulation with Ca2+ transients, demonstrating functionality. This biomaterial platform enables repeated, reliable study of Ca2+ communication within GBM tumor networks and testing of Ca2+-targeting therapeutics.

papers.title: Efficacy and safety of 15 mA transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) in the therapy of treatment-resistant depression with increased inflammatory activity: Study protocol for a randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial.
papers.summary: Protocol for a randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial of high-intensity (15 mA) transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) in treatment-resistant depression with elevated inflammatory activity (CRP 0.85-10 mg/L; DM-TRD >12.5), enrolling 70 participants. A 4-week intervention is followed by 8-week follow-up; the primary endpoint is MADRS change at week 4, with secondary EEG and peripheral-biomarker association analyses and safety monitoring.

papers.title: Lactylation: A central metabolic-epigenetic driver of sepsis-associated acute kidney injury.
papers.summary: Review framing protein lactylation — lactate modifying lysine residues — as a central metabolic-epigenetic hub in sepsis-associated acute kidney injury, governed by a dynamic writer-reader-eraser network. Lactylation reprograms immune responses (e.g., macrophage polarization), disrupts tubular mitochondrial function, and compromises microvascular integrity, acting cell-type and spatiotemporally specifically. H3K18 lactylation is a candidate diagnostic biomarker; the axis offers precision-therapy targets.

papers.title: tRNA-derived small RNAs in vascular smooth muscle cell phenotypic switching and vascular remodelling.
papers.summary: Review of tRNA-derived small RNAs (tsRNAs) in vascular smooth muscle cell phenotypic switching (contractile→synthetic) across atherosclerosis, aortic dissection, in-stent restenosis, and pulmonary hypertension. tsRNAs act bidirectionally: 5'-tiRNA-Cys-GCA and tRF-Glu-CTC suppress the synthetic phenotype and neointimal formation (via FMOD targeting), while tRF-Gln-CTG promotes it. A framework spanning transcriptional, post-transcriptional, and chromatin regulation is proposed; tsRNAs hold promise as liquid-biopsy biomarkers pending validation.

papers.title: Identification and differential expression analysis of Hfq-bound novel small RNAs in Serratia marcescens by nitrocellulose-based partitioning.
papers.summary: Hfq-associated small RNAs in Serratia marcescens were isolated by nitrocellulose membrane-based partitioning following Hfq overexpression and identified via high-throughput sequencing, yielding 159 novel sRNA candidates. Two — sm_hfq_NPC119 and sm_hfq_NPC07 — showed growth-phase-dependent expression; NPC119 (lag phase/biofilm) inversely correlates with type IV pilus pilW mRNA, while NPC07 (log phase) targets the type VI secretion tssB gene — potential anti-virulence targets.

papers.title: Trem2 regulates macrophage phenotype via the JAK2/STAT3 signaling pathway to ameliorate ventricular remodeling after acute myocardial infarction.
papers.summary: In a mouse acute myocardial infarction (AMI) model, Trem2 expression rose and peaked at the repair phase. Myeloid-specific Trem2 knockout worsened ventricular remodeling and cardiac dysfunction, suppressed JAK2/STAT3 activation, and skewed macrophages toward a pro-inflammatory phenotype. Exogenous sTrem2 restored pathway activity and improved cardiac function, while AG490 recapitulated dysfunction — the Trem2-JAK2/STAT3 axis regulates macrophage phenotype and is a promising post-AMI therapeutic target.

papers.title: Genetic dissection of inherited cold-stress reveals resilience hotspots in barley.
papers.summary: A three-generation field experiment using 138 barley accessions tested whether ancestral cold exposure produces inherited resilience. Memory-conditioned lineages outperformed the no-memory cold-stressed lineage: germination up from 79.0% to 83.5-86.6%, seedling survival from 68.0% to 77.7-85.5%, electrolyte leakage down, and grain yield per plant up from 4.27 g to 5.04-5.75 g; the integrated cold-resilience index rose from 38.9 to 49.8-58.9. GWAS (17,894 SNPs) found 137 significant marker-memory associations including germination loci on 5H and benefit-cost loci on 3H/6H.

papers.title: Graph-Aware Latent Representation Learning for Multimodal Spatial Omics Integration.
papers.journal: Omics : a journal of integrative biology
papers.summary: mmSPAO is a multimodal spatial omics fusion method integrating spatial transcriptomics, epigenomics, and proteomics via adjacency-graph modeling and latent spatial representation. It aligns modalities within shared spatial domains while preserving individual gene-expression profiles, producing globally integrated fusion maps that advance decoding of tissue architecture and cellular regulatory hierarchies, demonstrated on simulated and real multi-omics data.

papers.title: Large-Scale Cellular Phosphoproteomic Analysis Reveals a Putative Role for LPIN1 S162 in Metabolic Signaling.
papers.journal: Omics : a journal of integrative biology
papers.summary: Analysis of 99 differential cellular phosphoproteomics datasets identified LPIN1 S162 as the most frequently and consistently perturbed of 20 differentially regulated phosphosites. Co-occurrence and coregulation analyses link S162 to insulin signaling, AMPK signaling, autophagy, and metabolic adaptation, associating it with inhibitory IRS signaling and compensatory metabolic stress-response programs. Structural and evolutionary contexts argue S162 is a previously unrecognized regulatory phosphosite warranting direct experimental investigation.

papers.title: Ineffectual Genomic Error Correction Under Environmental Perturbation Dynamically Regulates Mutational Supply and Robustness.
papers.summary: The model shows that kinetic proofreading mechanics dictate replication fidelity, so environmental shifts alter the optimal proofreading driving rate, transiently elevating replication errors and triggering rapid evolution until a new fidelity optimum is reached — producing alternating stasis and adaptation (punctuated equilibrium). Coding-region length and population size jointly determine whether adaptation succeeds or mutational collapse occurs, consistent with the drift-barrier hypothesis on mutation-rate limits.
